tests.title: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is read fresh from GetVariableFunc on every sync and any value other than the exact string origin resolves to hub
given: a carry_patch workspace
a GetVariableFunc stub that records each call and returns a configurable value
tests.when: runCarryPatchSync is called twice in a row, first with the variable returning 'origin' then with it returning '' (unset)
then: GetVariable is called with ("workspace", slug, "PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE") on both calls
the first sync resolves to origin mode (fetches origin)
the second sync resolves to hub mode (no origin fetch) even though the first sync ran in origin mode
tests.pseudocode: cfg.GetVariable = recordingVar({"PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE":"origin"}); runCarryPatchSync(cfg,ctx1); assert originFetchCalled; cfg.GetVariable = recordingVar({"PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE":"weird"}); runCarryPatchSync(cfg,ctx2); assert !originFetchCalled

tests.title: PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is read only when PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is origin and any value other than the exact string report resolves to replace
given: a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
a diverged patch branch on origin
tests.when: sync runs with PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY unset, then with it set to 'weird'
then: GetVariable is called for PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY
the divergence is resolved by replace in both cases
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert patchesSynced[0].action == "replaced"

tests.title: Hub mode skips reading PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY and runs the origin fetch and fork-refresh as no-ops
given: a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset
then: GetVariable is never called for PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY
no origin fetch call is made
the fork-refresh step performs no ref writes
tests.pseudocode: runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert !calledWith(cfg.GetVariable, "PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY"); assert originFetchCallCount == 0

tests.title: A workspace that previously ran in origin mode reproduces the pre-spec sync behaviour and response shape once PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE is hub
given: a workspace whose last sync ran with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and left patches_synced state on disk
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE now unset
then: the response has no patches_synced field
origin_fetched is false
patches_merged and rebuild_triggered behave exactly as before this spec
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert resp.OriginFetched == false; assert !hasKey(resp,"patches_synced")

tests.title: Origin mode fetches the origin remote with the correct refspec, no tags, resolved auth, and the sync's wslock held
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
a successful upstream fetch
wslock held for the workspace slug
tests.when: sync proceeds past the upstream fetch
then: origin is fetched with refspec +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* and git.NoTags
the auth passed matches workspace.ResolveCloneAuth's resolution order
the fetch happens while wslock.TryLock's unlock has not yet been called
tests.pseudocode: spyFetch := recordingOriginFetch(); cfg.OriginFetch = spyFetch; runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert spyFetch.refspec == "+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*"; assert spyFetch.tags == NoTags; assert spyFetch.calledUnderLock

tests.title: A failing origin fetch aborts the sync with 502 and leaves the workspace row and every patches row unchanged
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
a stored upstream_head_sha, patch statuses and patch refs
an origin fetch stub that returns an error
then: the response status is 502
the error message is "origin fetch failed"
upstream_head_sha, last_sync_at, every patch's status and every patch ref are byte-for-byte identical to before the call
tests.pseudocode: before := snapshot(db, refs); r := post('/sync'); assert r.status == 502; assert r.json.message == "origin fetch failed"; assert snapshot(db, refs) == before

tests.title: An origin fetch error satisfying errors.Is(err, git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) is treated as success
given: PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin
an origin fetch stub returning git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate
then: the sync proceeds to the fork-refresh step instead of aborting
the response is not a 502
tests.pseudocode: cfg.OriginFetch = func(...) error { return git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate }; resp,err := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert err == nil; assert forkRefreshRan

tests.title: origin_fetched is true only when the origin fetch was attempted and succeeded, false in hub mode and on fetch failure
given: three syncs: hub mode, origin mode with success, origin mode with failure
then: hub-mode response has origin_fetched=false
successful origin-mode response has origin_fetched=true
the failing sync returns 502 (no response body to check but state unaffected)
tests.pseudocode: assert hubResp.OriginFetched == false; assert originResp.OriginFetched == true

tests.title: Only patches with status active, conflict or disabled are considered, in position order, excluding merged_upstream, deleted and the integration branch
given: patches with statuses active, conflict, disabled, merged_upstream, deleted, and one row whose branch_name equals the integration branch
tests.when: the fork-refresh step runs in origin mode
then: patches_synced contains an entry for each active/conflict/disabled patch in position order
no entry exists for the merged_upstream, deleted or integration-branch-named rows
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert [e.branch_name for e in resp.patches_synced] == expectedOrderedBranches

tests.title: A patch missing on origin leaves the local branch untouched, records missing_on_origin without changing status, and persists the state
given: an active patch whose refs/remotes/origin/<branch> does not exist after fetch
then: refs/heads/<branch> is not written
patches_synced has state missing_on_origin for that branch
the patch's status stays active
the patches row has origin_sync_state='missing_on_origin', origin_sha=null, origin_synced_at set
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); entry := findByBranch(resp.patches_synced, branch); assert entry.state == "missing_on_origin"; assert dbPatchStatus(branch) == "active"; assert dbPatch(branch).origin_sync_state == "missing_on_origin"

tests.title: A patch branch missing locally but present on origin is created at the origin tip via update-ref and counts as patch advanced
given: refs/remotes/origin/feature-x exists at SHA X
refs/heads/feature-x does not exist locally
then: update-ref creates refs/heads/feature-x at X, not checkout or reset
patches_synced records action created for feature-x
the branch counts as patch advanced for the rebuild decision
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert git.rev_parse("refs/heads/feature-x") == X; entry := findByBranch(resp.patches_synced,"feature-x"); assert entry.action == "created"; assert resp.RebuildTriggered == true

tests.title: A patch whose local and origin tips are the same commit is recorded in_sync with no ref write
given: refs/heads/feature-y and refs/remotes/origin/feature-y both point at SHA Y
then: no update-ref call is made for feature-y
patches_synced records state in_sync for feature-y
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert refUnchanged("refs/heads/feature-y"); entry := findByBranch(resp.patches_synced,"feature-y"); assert entry.state == "in_sync"

tests.title: A local tip that is an ancestor of the origin tip is fast-forwarded via update-ref using GitRunner.IsAncestor on resolved SHAs
given: refs/heads/feature-z at SHA A, refs/remotes/origin/feature-z at SHA B, A is an ancestor of B
then: IsAncestor is called with the resolved SHAs A and B, not branch names
update-ref moves refs/heads/feature-z to B
action fast_forwarded is recorded
the branch counts as patch advanced
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert git.rev_parse("refs/heads/feature-z") == B; entry := findByBranch(resp.patches_synced,"feature-z"); assert entry.action == "fast_forwarded"

tests.title: A diverged branch under replace policy is backed up to refs/hub/replaced, moved to the origin tip, and recorded as replaced with both SHAs
given: refs/heads/feature-w at SHA A, refs/remotes/origin/feature-w at SHA B, neither an ancestor of the other
PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=replace (default)
an existing refs/hub/replaced/feature-w from a prior replacement
then: refs/hub/replaced/feature-w is overwritten with A
refs/heads/feature-w is moved to B via update-ref
patches_synced records action replaced with local_sha=A, origin_sha=B, replaced_sha=A
the branch counts as patch advanced
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert git.rev_parse("refs/hub/replaced/feature-w") == A; assert git.rev_parse("refs/heads/feature-w") == B; entry := findByBranch(resp.patches_synced,"feature-w"); assert entry == {action:"replaced", local_sha:A, origin_sha:B, replaced_sha:A}

tests.title: A diverged branch under report policy is left untouched and recorded diverged with both SHAs
given: refs/heads/feature-v at SHA A, refs/remotes/origin/feature-v at SHA B, neither an ancestor of the other
PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report
then: refs/heads/feature-v is unchanged at A
no refs/hub/replaced ref is written
patches_synced records state diverged with local_sha=A and origin_sha=B
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert git.rev_parse("refs/heads/feature-v") == A; entry := findByBranch(resp.patches_synced,"feature-v"); assert entry.state == "diverged" and entry.local_sha==A and entry.origin_sha==B

tests.title: Moving the branch that is the trunk's current checkout runs git reset --hard to the new tip immediately after the ref move
given: the trunk clone's checked-out branch is feature-checked-out
its origin tip is ahead and fast-forwardable
then: update-ref moves the ref first
git reset --hard to the new tip runs immediately after
the working tree matches the new HEAD
tests.pseudocode: runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert git.calls contains ordered ["update-ref refs/heads/feature-checked-out <newsha>", "reset --hard <newsha>"]

tests.title: Sync returns early with empty patches_merged and rebuild_triggered false when upstream did not advance and no patch advanced
given: upstream fetch yields the same SHA as stored
origin mode with every patch already in_sync
then: patches_merged is empty
rebuild_triggered is false
no rebuild is enqueued
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert resp.PatchesMerged == []; assert resp.RebuildTriggered == false; assert queue.EnqueueCallCount == 0

tests.title: last_sync_at is updated on every error-free sync including the early-return no-op case
given: a workspace with an old last_sync_at
upstream unchanged and, in origin mode, no patch advanced
then: the workspace's last_sync_at in the database is updated to the current time
tests.pseudocode: before := dbLastSyncAt(slug); runCarryPatchSync(cfg); after := dbLastSyncAt(slug); assert after > before

tests.title: An auto-rebuild is enqueued with the existing group key and duplicate suppression when the sync did not return early and AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC is not the string false
given: a patch advanced under the fork-refresh step and upstream did not advance
AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC unset
then: a rebuild job is enqueued with group key slug+":"+integrationBranch
rebuild_triggered is true
a duplicate queued job for the same group is silently ignored on a second sync
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert resp.RebuildTriggered == true; assert queue.lastEnqueue.Group == slug+":"+integrationBranch

tests.title: Merge-upstream detection runs over branch tips as refreshed by the fork-refresh step, not their pre-sync tips
given: a patch branch that was fast-forwarded to a tip that is now an ancestor of the new upstream HEAD, but whose pre-sync tip was not
then: the merge-upstream detection loop reports this patch as merged, because it checks the post-refresh tip
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert branch in resp.PatchesMerged

tests.title: origin_fetched is present as a boolean in every sync response regardless of PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE
given: a hub-mode sync and an origin-mode sync
then: both response bodies include an origin_fetched boolean field
tests.pseudocode: assert typeof(hubResp.OriginFetched) == bool; assert typeof(originResp.OriginFetched) == bool

tests.title: In origin mode, patches_synced has one shaped element per considered patch with replaced_sha present only for a replaced action
given: origin mode with one created, one fast_forwarded and one replaced patch
then: patches_synced has exactly three elements
each element has branch_name, action, state, local_sha, origin_sha
only the replaced element carries replaced_sha
action values are drawn from {none, created, fast_forwarded, replaced} and state from {in_sync, diverged, missing_on_origin}
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert len(resp.patches_synced) == 3; for e in resp.patches_synced: assert hasKey(e,"branch_name") and hasKey(e,"action") and hasKey(e,"state"); assert hasKey(replacedEntry, "replaced_sha"); assert !hasKey(createdEntry, "replaced_sha")

tests.title: In hub mode, the sync response omits patches_synced entirely
given: a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset
then: the response body has no patches_synced key at all
tests.pseudocode: resp := post('/sync'); assert !hasKey(resp.json, "patches_synced")

tests.title: Under report policy, patches_diverged lists the branch names recorded diverged during this sync
given: PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=report
two branches diverge and one is in_sync
then: patches_diverged contains exactly the two diverged branch names and no others
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert sorted(resp.patches_diverged) == sorted(["branch-a","branch-b"])

tests.title: Under replace policy, patches_diverged is present and empty even when a divergence was resolved
given: PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY=replace (default)
one branch diverges and is replaced
then: the response includes patches_diverged as an array
the array is empty
the replaced branch's name is not present in it
tests.pseudocode: resp := runCarryPatchSync(cfg); assert resp.patches_diverged == []

tests.title: Schema migration adds nullable origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at columns to the patches table idempotently
given: a patches table without the new columns
a second database that already has them
tests.when: initSchema (or the equivalent migration entrypoint) runs against both
then: the first database gains the three nullable columns
the second database's migration is a no-op and does not error
existing rows keep the three new columns null
tests.pseudocode: initSchema(dbWithout); assert columnsOf(dbWithout,"patches") contains ["origin_sync_state","origin_sha","origin_synced_at"]; initSchema(dbWith); assert noError

tests.title: Switching to hub mode clears origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at to null for every non-deleted patch of the workspace
given: a workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE now unset
several non-deleted patches carrying non-null origin_sync_state/origin_sha/origin_synced_at from a prior origin-mode sync
one soft-deleted patch also carrying stale fork state
then: every non-deleted patch's three fork-sync columns are null after the sync
the soft-deleted patch's columns are left untouched
tests.pseudocode: runCarryPatchSync(cfg); for p in nonDeletedPatches(slug): assert p.origin_sync_state == nil and p.origin_sha == nil and p.origin_synced_at == nil; assert deletedPatch.origin_sync_state == priorValue

tests.title: GET and PATCH patch endpoints expose the three fork-sync fields, null when unset, matching the upstream_pr_url convention
given: one patch with origin_sync_state/origin_sha/origin_synced_at set and one with them unset
tests.when: GET /workspaces/:slug/patches, GET /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id and PATCH /workspaces/:slug/patches/:id are called for both patches
then: the set patch's response carries the three fields with their stored values
the unset patch's response carries the three fields as null (or omitted), matching how upstream_pr_url is represented when unset
tests.pseudocode: r1 := get('/patches/'+setPatchID); assert r1.json.origin_sync_state == "in_sync"; r2 := get('/patches/'+unsetPatchID); assert r2.json.origin_sync_state == nil

tests.title: GET /workspaces/:slug/patch-status includes the three fork-sync fields per patch and adds patches_diverged and patches_missing_on_origin summary counts
given: patches with origin_sync_state values in_sync, diverged, diverged, missing_on_origin, and null
then: each patch entry in the response carries origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at
summary.patches_diverged equals 2
summary.patches_missing_on_origin equals 1
tests.pseudocode: r := get('/patch-status'); assert r.json.summary.patches_diverged == 2; assert r.json.summary.patches_missing_on_origin == 1

tests.title: A sync in origin mode emits one hub.patch.sync event with per-category branch lists, plus one hub.patch.replace event per replaced branch
given: a fake audit.Emitter
an origin-mode sync producing one created, one fast_forwarded and one replaced branch
then: exactly one hub.patch.sync event is emitted with actor type system, resource type patch, and metadata created/fast_forwarded/replaced/diverged/missing_on_origin listing the right branch names
exactly one hub.patch.replace event is emitted for the replaced branch, carrying its name and both SHAs
tests.pseudocode: runCarryPatchSync(cfg); events := fakeEmitter.Events; syncEvt := find(events,"hub.patch.sync"); assert syncEvt.ActorType=="system" and syncEvt.ResourceType=="patch" and syncEvt.Metadata.created==[...]; replaceEvt := find(events,"hub.patch.replace"); assert replaceEvt.Metadata.branch_name=="feature-w"

tests.title: A nil audit emitter or a failing Emit call does not affect the sync's response or state changes
given: two syncs identical except Audit is nil in one and an Emit-erroring fake in the other
then: both complete with the same HTTP status and response body content aside from timestamps/ids
both leave the same patch and workspace state
the erroring emitter's error is only logged, not surfaced to the caller
tests.pseudocode: r1 := runCarryPatchSync(cfgNilAudit); r2 := runCarryPatchSync(cfgErrAudit); assert r1.err == nil and r2.err == nil; assert responsesEquivalent(r1,r2)

tests.title: A fork-only patch branch is created by sync, triggers a rebuild, and shows up on the patch-status dashboard
given: a real carry-patch workspace with a trunk clone, origin and upstream remotes
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin set as a workspace variable
a new patch branch pushed to the fork only, registered as a patch row
then: the sync response has origin_fetched=true, patches_synced containing the branch with action created, and rebuild_triggered=true
refs/heads/<branch> now exists locally at the fork's tip
a hub.patch.sync audit event was recorded
the patch-status response shows the patch's origin_sync_state and updated summary counts
real_components: git runner against a real repository

tests.title: A diverged patch branch is replaced under the default divergence policy, backing up the hub's tip and triggering a rebuild
given: a real carry-patch workspace in origin mode
a registered patch branch whose hub copy and force-pushed fork copy have diverged
PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY left at its default
then: refs/hub/replaced/<branch> now holds the old local tip
refs/heads/<branch> now points at the fork's tip
hub.patch.replace and hub.patch.sync audit events were recorded
the sync response's patches_synced has the replaced entry and rebuild_triggered=true
the patches row persists origin_sync_state/origin_sha/origin_synced_at
real_components: git runner against a real repository

tests.title: A hub-mode workspace is unaffected by this spec and clears stale fork-sync state left from a prior origin-mode run
given: a real carry-patch workspace that previously synced with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and has patches carrying non-null origin_sync_state
PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE now left unset
then: the sync response has origin_fetched=false and no patches_synced field
last_sync_at is updated even though upstream did not advance
every patch's origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at are null in the GET response
real_components: git runner against a real repository
